root_cause: Existing provider evidence can show a failed configuration mutation or an intentionally anonymous-callable privileged RPC while the deployment itself is healthy. These are distinct unresolved controls: a ready deploy and a token-checking function body alone do not establish closure.
fix: Expand the existing Security Agent roster and same-lineage skill with bounded denial handling, owner escalation for unsupported provider control-plane actions, source-consumer tracing before any privileged permission change and independent negative-access/provider-advisor proof. Continue original Heartbeat, protected writer and private incident observation channel. This policy amendment is not a claim that either provider vulnerability was fixed.
prevention_rules: A 4xx/unsupported provider mutation may not be interpreted as a successful access-control setting change or indefinitely retried.
Escalate an inaccessible provider control to the original owner and retain FAIL until both protected-setting readback and anonymous-denial proof succeed.
Investigate all privileged RPC callers and credential rotation before any revoke or change of backend execution rights.
A database advisor WARN persists until the original provider independently reports remediation and existing authorized calls still work.
Keep security incidents and source evidence private, deduplicated and expiring; plain-language customer trust status must not expose diagnostics.
Every release and changed skill needs original Required/CodeQL/full BRAIN gates and exact main and production readback; no parallel agent or bypass.
owner: existing ONE BRAIN Security Agent under exclusive writer
